The table presented defines the keyword “CLOA” and its associated parameters for managing the activation and deactivation of load groups during staged construction analysis. CLOA itself “references a load group that has previously been defined and stored in a separate load case and activates it for the current construction stage.” Once a group is activated by CLOA, it remains in effect for all subsequent stages until it is explicitly deactivated—except when the TEMP option is used, which confines activation to the present stage only. Users often cross‐reference this functionality with related commands such as CS, CSYS and CCRL when setting up coordinate systems, load cases or construction stages.

The table is organized into four columns—Item, Description, Unit and Default—and three main entries (rows). Below is a detailed breakdown:

1. Item: NO  
   • Description: Number of referenced load case  
   • Unit: — (no physical unit required)  
   • Default: “!” (an exclamation mark indicates this field is mandatory)  
   This first parameter tells the solver which previously defined load case index to reference. The user must supply a valid load‐case number here; no default numerical value is assumed.

2. Item: OPT  
   • Description: Action of group  
   • Unit: LIT (literal string)  
   • Default: ACT  
   Under OPT, the user specifies one of three literal options:  
     – ACT : Activation. Permanently turns on the referenced load group from this stage onward.  
     – DEAC: Deactivation of load group. Permanently turns off the referenced load group from this stage onward.  
     – TEMP: Temporary activation for the current stage only. After completion of the stage, the group reverts to its prior state (active or inactive).  
   By default, if the user omits OPT, the system assumes “ACT,” meaning the load group will be activated and remain so until a later DEAC call overrides it.

3. Item: FACT  
   • Description: Factor for the loads  
   • Unit: — (a dimensionless multiplier)  
   • Default: 1.0  
   This parameter allows the user to scale the entire load group by a constant factor. A default value of 1.0 implies no scaling; values above or below unity uniformly amplify or reduce the applied loads.

Additional hint: If “TEMP” is chosen for OPT, the activation applies strictly to the current construction stage—subsequent stages revert to whatever activation state existed before the TEMP call. Otherwise, groups activated by ACT persist indefinitely until explicitly deactivated by DEAC.

See also:  
– CS (Construction Stage definitions)  
– CSYS (Coordinate System assignments)  
– CCRL (Construction Case or Related Load definitions)  

Together, these controls give the user fine‐grained mastery over which load collections are in force at each stage of a construction‐sequence simulation, enabling accurate modeling of staged builds, load application, and structural response.

See also: CS, CSYS, CCRL
 CLOA
 CLOA references a load group that has previously been defined and stored in a separate load case and activates it for the current construction stage.
 Hint
 Once activated, the load group remains active also for subsequent construction stages as long as it is not explicitly deactivated (exception: OPT TEMP)!

The input table under discussion defines the three parameters available for the “CGW” (groundwater) record in the software’s input deck.  CGW is used to impose a global phreatic (groundwater) surface across all active element groups in a model.  These settings remain in effect for all subsequent construction or analysis stages unless explicitly changed by another CGW record.  In some cases users may specify a simple horizontal groundwater level; in other situations they may wish to reference a previously computed hydraulic potential distribution.  The table makes it clear which items you must supply, what they mean, what units are expected, and what defaults (if any) will apply.

1. Columns and Their Significance  
   - Item: the mnemonic or keyword that the user types on the CGW line (HW, LC, or T).  
   - Description: a brief explanation of what that keyword represents.  
   - Unit: the physical unit in which the value must be given.  Numerical subscripts (e.g. m₁₀₀₆) indicate the internal unit code used by the software; these are chiefly relevant for ensuring consistency and for checking dimensionally correct input.  
   - Default: the value assumed by the program if you omit the item.  In this table all defaults are “–” to indicate that the user must explicitly supply HW, LC, and T if they intend to use that mode of specifying groundwater.

2. Table Rows Explained  
   • HW (Ground water level)  
     – Description: Specifies a single horizontal phreatic surface by giving its global coordinate along the gravity (vertical) axis.  Positive values of HW are measured downward in the direction of gravity (so an HW of 10.00 [m] means the phreatic surface lies ten meters below the datum in the gravity direction).  
     – Unit: [m]₁₀₀₆ (meters in the software’s unit coding).  
     – Default: none; if the user wants a simple horizontal level, they must provide HW.  

   • LC (Load Case Number)  
     – Description: References an existing hydraulic load case that contains a distribution of hydraulic potentials (phreatic surfaces that vary spatially).  When LC is supplied, the program retrieves the potential distribution from the specified load case rather than using a constant HW throughout.  
     – Unit: “—” (unitless, since this is an index identifying one of the user’s previously defined load cases).  
     – Default: none; LC must be provided if you wish to use a potential-based groundwater definition.  

   • T (Reference Time)  
     – Description: When LC is specified, T gives the time point within that load case at which you want to read the hydraulic potential distribution.  This allows you to apply transient or staged groundwater conditions exactly as they were computed earlier.  
     – Unit: [sec]₁₂₉₀ (seconds in the software’s unit coding).  
     – Default: none; T must be provided along with LC.

3. Usage Notes and Cross-References  
   – If both HW and (LC, T) are defined on the same CGW record, the software typically gives priority to the potential‐based specification (LC, T), but you should consult the “PHRS” record description for exact precedence rules.  
   – The phreatic surface set by CGW applies to all active element groups from that construction stage onward until it is overwritten by another CGW record.  
   – See also:  
     • CS / CSYS for coordinate‐system definitions that affect where HW is measured.  
     • CCRL for coupling with consolidation or seepage‐consolidation load cases.  
     • PHRS for further details on storing and retrieving hydraulic potential distributions across time.

See also: CS, CSYS, CCRL, PHRS
 CGW
 CGW defines a global phreatic surface that is accounted for by all active element groups. It is possible to define a horizontal phreatic level by specifying the corresponding ordinate HW on the gravity axis; alternatively, a hydraulic potential distribution can be referenced via load case number LC and time T (for details, please refer to record PHRS).
 The ground water level settings remain valid also for subsequent construction stages as long as they are not changed explicitly!

See also: CS
 CTXT
 Item Description Unit Default Text line LT72 -
 CTXT allows the definition of a text string that is passed through to the CSG generated calcu- lation file. The insertion point is determined by the position of the CTXT command within the definition of the construction stage sequence. Enclosing inverted commas prevent a possible interpretation by the parser, which allows, e.g., passing through of commentary lines.
 ...
 CTXT ! Now a file is included:
 CTXT '#include system_sketch.draw'
 CS NO 1 TITL 'In-situ state'
 CS NO 1 TITL ‘In-situ state'
 ...

The table defines the syntax and semantics of the ECHO command’s keyword‐arguments—OPT, VAL, FROM, TO and INC—for controlling what finite‐element data get “echoed” (i.e. written out) into your RAG vector store.  Below is a walk‐through of each column and every allowable setting:

1. Columns  
   • Item  
     – Name of the keyword (OPT, VAL, FROM, TO, INC) that may appear in the ECHO command.  
   • Description  
     – A brief English summary of what the keyword does and the valid literals or numbers it accepts.  
   • Unit  
     – Indicates whether the argument is a literal token (LIT) or a numerical sequence (integer).  
   • Default  
     – The value assumed if you omit that keyword.

2. OPT  (Unit = LIT, Default = “*”)  
   • Purpose: Selects which categories of model data to echo.  
   • You must supply one of these literals (case‐insensitive).  If you give “*”, it is shorthand for “FULL” (i.e. all categories).  
   • Valid literals and their meanings (default state in parentheses when “*” is used):  
     – NODE: node‐point parameters (NO)  
     – MAT: material properties (NO)  
     – ELEM: element connectivity & geometry (NO)  
     – BOUN: boundary‐element definitions (NO)  
     – LOAD: applied loads (YES)  
     – DEFO: initial displacements (NO)  
     – STRE: element‐level stress/strain results (NO)  
     – BEDD: bedding‐soil stresses (NO)  
     – REAC: reaction & coupling forces at supports (NO)  
     – LINE: distributed support reactions along edges (YES)  
     – RESI: residual forces at each iteration (YES)  
     – NOST: nodal averages of element results (NO)  
     – ERIN: a-posteriori error estimates (OFF)  
     – STAT: statistical summaries at material integration points (YES)  
     – CSPL: plot‐switch for constructive solid geometry mode (YES)  
     – CSIG: fiber‐beam cross‐section stress distributions (NO)  
     – FULL: all of the above categories  

3. VAL  (Unit = LIT, Default = FULL)  
   • Purpose: Controls the verbosity of the echo operation—how much detail to produce.  
   • Valid options:  
     – OFF: no calculation or output at all  
     – NO: skip output (but still calculate)  
     – YES: generate the standard, minimal output  
     – FULL: extended details (default)  
     – EXTR: maximum, “extreme” verbosity  
     – 4: special mode for OPT=LOAD—only echoes loads on nodes that can move  

4. FROM  (Unit = integer or certain literals, Default = “!”)  
   • Purpose: Defines the starting index (or group name) of the selection sequence you wish to echo.  
   • Can be a positive integer designating a previously defined sequence number or the literal GRP to echo entire groups.  
   • If omitted, “!” indicates “start from the first available” by default.

5. TO  (Unit = integer, Default = same as FROM)  
   • Purpose: Sets the end index (or group number) of the echo range.  
   • If you only want one sequence, omit TO and it defaults to the same value as FROM.  

6. INC  (Unit = integer, Default = 1)  
   • Purpose: Specifies the step size between sequence numbers when echoing a range from FROM up to TO.  
   • For example, INC=2 would echo every second sequence in the specified span.

See also:  
• CTRL – high‐level control statements  
• SYST – system‐level echo settings  
• GRP  – group definitions used by FROM/TO  
• LC   – loop constructs that can drive ECHO calls  

In practice, a minimal ECHO line might look like:  
ECHO OPT=LOAD,REAC VAL=YES FROM=1 TO=5 INC=2  
– This prints only loads and reactions, with regular verbosity, for sequences 1, 3, and 5.

The internal forces and stresses are printed for each QUAD element at the element center (ECHO STRE YES). Additional output of the element reactions at the integration points is obtained by requesting ECHO STRE FULL.
 The internal forces for each beam element are printed at its beginning and at its end.
 The displacements and the axial forces are printed for all spring and truss elements.

For each node, internal forces or stresses of adjacent QUAD-elements are averaged and stored in the database.
 Averaging of the internal forces occurs group-wise, accounting for the groups defined at sys- tem generation. Subgroups are formed automatically at nodes at which the thickness of the bordering elements or the material number do not correspond. Hence, two or more results at one node may be generated even within one group.

For boundaries that have been assigned a name, the calculated distributed reaction forces are printed. ECHO LINE YES only provides for the sums of the boundaries, while ECHO LINE FULL additionally triggers printout of the boundary-associated nodal reactions.
For non-linear calculations, by default the maximum residual forces per iteration are provided in as an iteration log. The iteration log is suppressed by specifying ECHO RESI NO.

When running problems with non-linear material response, the option ECHO STAT provides the possibility of output of material point statistics for all non-linear QUAD integration points. These statistics contain information like, e.g., the number of linearly/ nonlinearly loaded integration points and the number of integration points that have reached the tension/ compression limit or the apex.
 Defining ECHO STAT YES provides for summarizing statistics at the end of the respective load case. ECHO STAT NO suppresses this output. ECHO STAT EXTR effects output after each iteration step. This option may help to track or localize convergence problems.

For the option CSIG, an optional selection set can be specified. Two possibilities exist:
 • Direct selection of elements or an element sequence via the element ID’s. Example: ECHO CSIG FROM 1 TO 10 INC 1 selects all elements with ID’s in the range of 1 to 10.
 • Selection of elements via primary or secondary group affiliation. Example: ECHO CSIG GRP ’A2’ selects all elements belonging to (secondary) group A2.
